issues.main_description_html:
• improve website inputs validation at Image Processing submission is only for non Pay as you go accounts
  • Set Website Profile data https://360photographers.org/photographer/youcef-pnl-e3lc to null

Result by Developer

The fix for this is in the frontend, and no backend or data change is needed.

Why the website showed: the profile page made it up. /photographer/youcef-pnl-e3lc already returns "website": null from the API (subscription 100, Pay as you go), but the frontend fell back to https://<slug>-360.com whenever a profile had no website, so it displayed youcef-pnl-e3lc-360.com. Every profile without a website, paid or not, showed a fake link like that.

The two checklist items:

  • Website validation for Pay as you go: it's already enforced in two places. The profile update here (updatePhotographerProfile.go) rejects a website unless the subscription is Basic, Pro or Agency, and the dashboard hides the website field for Pay as you go accounts. The apply/submission endpoint doesn't accept a website at all.
  • Set the website for youcef-pnl-e3lc to null: it's already null in the database.

Fix: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#95 (PR GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#96, released in GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#97). The Website row only appears when the profile actually has a website. It's merged to master and will show on 360photographers.org after the next frontend deploy.

issues.display_title: Issue #35: Fix Issue Photographer Location Endpoint Returns Stale Sublocations (Max 4 Shows Only 3)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 19/06/26

✅ Implementation Complete — Ready for Unit Testing

Summary

The GET /v1/photographers/{gothruUserId}/location endpoint returns a stale list of sublocations. A photographer can have up to 4 sublocations, but the endpoint keeps returning the previous cached value (e.g. 3) after a new sublocation is added.

Root cause

This is a cache invalidation bug, not a data-retrieval bug.

  • The location controller caches the response under photographer:v*:location:<gothruUserId> (helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerLocation).
  • When a sublocation is added (AddSublocation) or updated (UpdateSublocation), the cache invalidation cleared the detail, geodata, count, and markers patterns — but not the location pattern (PhotographerLocationPattern).
  • Result: the detail endpoint reflects 4 sublocations, while the location endpoint keeps serving the stale cached value (3) until the TTL expires.

The invalidation pattern (PhotographerLocationPattern, photographer:v*:location:<id>) already exists in helpers/redis_keys.go; it was simply never invoked from the sublocation mutations.

Fix

Add PhotographerLocationPattern invalidation, keyed by photographer.GothruUserID (the location cache is keyed by gothru user id only), in both mutation actions:

  • src/action/v1/sublocations/addSublocation.go
  • src/action/v1/sublocations/updateSublocation.go
_, _ = helpers.ClearRedisKeys(helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerLocationPattern(photographer.GothruUserID))

The v* wildcard in the pattern covers all cache versions.

GetPhotographerLocation (action + controller) needs no change — its query is correct (Find with no limit, no soft-delete on the model).

Verification

  • go build ./src/action/v1/sublocations/ passes.
  • Manual: add a 4th sublocation, then call the location endpoint — it now returns 4 immediately instead of the stale 3.

Out of scope (noted, not changed)

The DB column is misspelled latilatitude (mapped in models/directory_photographer_sublocation.go and referenced by raw SQL in getBulkCityPhotographerCounts.go and getPhotographerCount.go). Renaming it requires a DB migration plus updating all references; left as-is to avoid breaking production queries.

Relates to #28, #29.

Feedback

The link in the email is missing the photographer in the URL.

The "your photographer profile is now live" email renders:

The malformed link is therefore coming from either:

  • the Plunk email template (base URL + {{slug}} joined without the photographer path segment), or
  • whatever service actually triggers/sends the approval email (likely gothru-dashboard).

First step for the assignee: locate where the profile URL string is assembled, then fix the path.

  • Verified with a real approval email to a test inbox — the link opens the photographer's live profile.
  • Fix applied at the source (template or sender), with the correct base path documented.

Root cause: profileUrl built as %s/%s (base + slug) — missing /photographer segment.

Description

To increase the directory's credibility, we are introducing a feature where photographers can request reviews from their clients via a shareable link. To prevent spam, clients must authenticate via LinkedIn before submitting a review.

Feedback (source)

What people would like is to send a review link to a client and have that client fill it in. So maybe we can implement a sharable link in their profile that will be only for capturing the review from the client. But to me, in order to leave a review, you should have a LinkedIn account — and you should be doing that via the LinkedIn connection.

What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

This repo already has an email → code → submit review flow:

  • Model DirectoryReview with code, is_code_valid, and a 24h validity window.
  • src/action/v1/reviews/sendEmailReview.go — emails a review code to a client.
  • src/action/v1/reviews/getReviewByCode.go — GetReviewByCode(code) validates the code.
  • src/action/v1/reviews/addReview.go — AddReview(code, req) submits the review, updates the photographer rating, invalidates caches.

Gaps this task fills:

  1. The current link is a per-email, single-use, 24h code — not a reusable shareable link the photographer can put in their profile.
  2. AddReview has no authentication — anyone with a code can submit, and name is free-text. There is no LinkedIn gate.

Sub-tasks (Backend — foundation)

  1. Shareable review link: Add an endpoint/mechanism so each photographer has a stable, shareable review link tied to their profile (resolves to the photographer; not a one-time 24h email code). Decide reuse vs. new token model around DirectoryReview.
  2. LinkedIn OAuth integration: Add LinkedIn auth (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) so a client signs in with LinkedIn before reviewing. Capture verified identity (name, LinkedIn id/profile) from the provider rather than free-text.
  3. Gate review submission: Require a valid authenticated LinkedIn session/token on the submit endpoint (AddReview). Reject unauthenticated submissions.
  4. Anti-spam / dedupe: Use the verified LinkedIn identity to prevent duplicate or spam reviews per photographer.
  5. Config & secrets: Add LinkedIn client id/secret + redirect URI via env (src/config/environment.go), documented in README.

Open questions (resolve at pickup)

  • Reuse the existing code column for the shareable link, or introduce a separate per-photographer share token?
  • Should the LinkedIn-verified reviewer name/avatar replace the current free-text name?
  • One review per LinkedIn identity per photographer, or allow updates?
  • Privacy/storage policy for LinkedIn data (what we persist vs. only verify).

Acceptance criteria

  • A photographer has a stable shareable review link associated with their profile.
  • Opening the link requires the client to authenticate via LinkedIn before the review form is usable.
  • Review submission endpoint rejects requests without a valid LinkedIn-authenticated session.
  • Submitted reviews carry the verified LinkedIn identity; spam/duplicate submissions are blocked.
  • LinkedIn credentials configured via env; flow documented in README.
  • Existing rating recalculation + cache invalidation continue to work.

Note: this is the API foundation — frontend (profile share UI, LinkedIn login button, review form) is tracked separately.

issues.main_description_html:
Feature: Photographer Update Notification Email
Effort: L | Optional (decision A2) | Labels: backend, worker, infra
Files: action (edit to publish), cmd/workers/photographerUpdateWorker/main.go (new), Makefile (edit)

Move sending off the request path. Action publishes to maps_photographer_update (legacy JSON envelope); new worker (copy visibilityWorker) consumes and calls helpers.SendEmail. Register binary in Makefile build target.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Endpoint returns 202 immediately; email sent by worker.
  • Worker tolerates malformed messages; logs failures.
  • make build produces the new binary.

Depends on: TASK-3, TASK-4.
Ref: brainstorm/brainstorming-api.md TASK-5

Testing Scenario

  • Non-blocking: Endpoint publishes to maps_photographer_update and returns 202 immediately (no wait on Plunk).
  • Worker delivers (integration): Worker consumes the message and the email arrives in a test inbox.
  • Malformed message: Bad/undecodable payload → worker logs error and does NOT crash; message handled (ack/nack) per existing worker pattern.
  • Queue wiring: maps_photographer_update queue is declared/bound; legacy JSON envelope matches other workers.
  • Build: make build produces the photographerUpdateWorker binary.
  • Broker resilience: Worker survives a RabbitMQ restart / reconnects.

RESULT

❌ Not Planned — Superseded by Plunk

Async email queuing via RabbitMQ worker is no longer required. Plunk already handles email delivery queuing internally, making a separate photographerUpdateWorker redundant.

The synchronous helpers.SendEmail call in NotifyPhotographerUpdate runs inside a goroutine (non-blocking), so the request path is not affected by Plunk latency.

Decision: skip RabbitMQ queue + worker for this feature. Closing as not planned.
